We need to determine number of C=O groups in the compound. We have no structure given. We need to infer from NMR or IR? Could use IR spectra to detect carbonyl stretch. Use ir_spectra tool (expensive). But maybe we can get carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-220 ppm). Could also use retrieve_carbon_shifts to know typical ranges. But we need actual compound; we don't have SMILES. Possibly the system has a sample at hand (the compound). We need to measure IR to see carbonyl peaks. Use ir_spectra tool (costly but okay). Then count number of C=O peaks (strong ~1700-1750 cm-1). Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl signals. Use carbon_nmr_spectra. That returns list of shifts. Count those in carbonyl range (~190-220 ppm for ketones, ~160-185 for esters, amides). Might be ambiguous.

Simplest: use ir_spectra and count peaks around 1700 cm-1. Let's call ir_spectra.
